The facade is packed with detail: ornate spires, intricate stonework and Gaudí’s signature organic forms that blur the line between architecture and sculpture. It’s one of the most visited buildings on earth, and surprisingly hard to find as a physical model.

A striking display piece for anyone who loves Barcelona, Gaudí, or sacred architecture — and a great addition to any world landmark collection.

title: 1959 Retro Radio Replica – Mid-Century Design Icon | 3D Printed
description:
This 3D-printed replica brings home one of the most celebrated objects of 20th-century industrial design — a 1959 portable radio-phonograph that helped define the minimalist ‘less but better’ aesthetic.

The original combined a transistor radio and a record player in one portable unit, and remains a touchstone of modernist design. Its circular dial and perforated speaker grille are widely cited as influences on later iconic product design, including Apple’s iPod.

Printed at approximately 18cm tall in your choice of 13 colours. A great display piece for design fans, mid-century enthusiasts, or anyone who appreciates clean industrial form.

title: Château de Chambord (Central Keep) – Loire Valley | 3D Printed Landmark
description:
This 3D-printed model captures the central keep of the Château de Chambord — the showpiece of French Renaissance architecture in the heart of the Loire Valley. The real château rises to 56 metres at its lantern tower, the tallest point of the keep, and was begun in 1519 for Francis I with a design said to be touched by Leonardo da Vinci.

The keep is famous for its extraordinary roofline — eleven different kinds of tower, three styles of chimney, and not a hint of symmetry — which Henry James said looked “more like the spires of a city than the salient points of a single building.” Inside the real keep, the celebrated double-helix staircase ascends three floors without the two spirals ever meeting.

A striking display piece for anyone who loves the Loire, French history, or Renaissance architecture — and a great addition to a world landmark collection.

description:

Designed by Richard Seifert and opened in 1981, the building’s three-leaf plan was famously said to mirror the old NatWest logo when viewed from above (something the architect always denied). The model captures that distinctive cantilevered profile with the three projecting wings extending from the central core.

A solid pick for a London skyline collection — sits naturally alongside the Gherkin, Cheesegrater and Walkie Talkie in any City of London display.

title: Santa Ana Cathedral (Facade) – El Salvador | 3D Printed Landmark
description:
This 3D-printed model captures the striking neo-Gothic facade of the Cathedral of Our Lady Saint Anne in Santa Ana, El Salvador. With its twin bell towers, ornate entrance doors and Gothic tracery, it’s one of Central America’s most distinctive cathedrals — and you almost never see it offered as a physical model.

Originally built between 1906 and 1959, the real cathedral stands as a rare example of Gothic Revival architecture in El Salvador, where most churches follow a Spanish colonial style. This model covers the full front elevation including both towers, the rose window and the central Puerta del Perdón.

Available in three sizes:
• Small – 15 cm tall, 12 cm wide. A compact desk or shelf piece.
• Medium – 20 cm tall, 16 cm wide. A solid mid-size display model.
• Large – 25 cm tall, 20 cm wide. The largest option — real presence on a shelf or mantelpiece.
